scene.headline: Adobe ends Creative Suite, goes subscription-only

lines.say: Before, the full Creative Suite cost twenty-five ninety-nine, once. After, Creative Cloud cost about fifty dollars a month.

lines.text: $2,599 / $49.99 = about 52 months. Then it keeps going.
lines.say: Do the math, and the rent passes the old price in about fifty-two months, then just keeps going.

lines.text: Subscription revenue: $11.6B in fiscal 2020 to $22.9B in fiscal 2025.
lines.say: That's why Adobe's subscription revenue grew from about eleven point six billion dollars in fiscal twenty twenty to twenty-two point nine billion in fiscal twenty twenty-five.

lines.text: Signed but not yet counted: $22.52B, as of Nov. 28, 2025.
lines.say: On top of that, it had about twenty-two and a half billion dollars in signed contracts it hadn't counted yet.
And since sending you one more copy costs almost nothing, its gross margin was about eighty-nine percent.
The lesson for you: fifty dollars a month is about six hundred a year, so know what you're renting.

post.title: 96% of Adobe's Revenue Is Subscriptions. Here's Why
post.ig:
96% of Adobe's revenue is basically rent.
In 2013, Adobe swapped the $2,599 Creative Suite for Creative Cloud at $49.99 a month.
Subscription revenue grew from $11.6B in fiscal 2020 to $22.9B in fiscal 2025.
It also had $22.52B in signed contracts not yet counted as revenue (as of Nov. 28, 2025), and an 89% gross margin.
Sources: Adobe 10-K filings FY2021-FY2025, TechCrunch (May 2013).
